#!/bin/bash

# Database Credentials Prompt Script

echo "Please enter your database connection details:"

# Prompt for database host
read -p "Database host (default: localhost): " db_host
if [ -z "$db_host" ]; then
    db_host="localhost"
fi

# Prompt for database port
read -p "Database port (default: 5432): " db_port
if [ -z "$db_port" ]; then
    db_port="5432"
fi

# Prompt for database name
read -p "Database name: " db_name
while [ -z "$db_name" ]; do
    echo "Database name cannot be empty."
    read -p "Database name: " db_name
done

# Prompt for database user
read -p "Database user: " db_user
while [ -z "$db_user" ]; do
    echo "Database user cannot be empty."
    read -p "Database user: " db_user
done

# Prompt for database password (hidden input)
echo -n "Database password: "
# Use stty to hide password input
stty -echo
read db_password
stty echo
echo "" # Print newline after password input

# Optional: Confirm the connection details
echo "\nConnection details:\nHost: $db_host\nPort: $db_port\nDatabase: $db_name\nUser: $db_user"

# Note: Password is not displayed for security reasons

# Here you would typically use these variables to connect to the database
# For example, with psql:
# PGPASSWORD="$db_password" psql -h "$db_host" -p "$db_port" -U "$db_user" "$db_name"

# Or with mysql:
# mysql -h "$db_host" -P "$db_port" -u "$db_user" -p"$db_password" "$db_name"

# Unset the password variable for security
unset db_password

echo "\nScript completed. Password has been unset for security."
